newsitem.title: FRANCE: Louvre reopens after talks begin in labour dispute.
newsitem.headline: Louvre reopens after talks begin in labour dispute.

text.p: The Louvre museum, one of the French capital's top tourist attractions, reopened on Monday after striking guards ended a five-day blockade in exchange for a promise of talks with management over their grievances.

The strikers had been blocking the museum's ultra-modern glass pyramid entrance, disappointing thousands of art lovers and tourists hoping to glimpse such works as the Mona Lisa, the Venus de Milo and the Winged Victory of Samothrace.
The guards, who work the night shift in the museum, are demanding 28 nights off each year instead of the 26 offered by management.

Management accused the pickets of taking tourists and art lovers hostage, noting that they represent only a fraction of the 1,000 or so guards in the vast museum. The Louvre normally receives about 18,000 visitors a day in May.
